morphology.shape: Spherical, enveloped virion with icosahedral capsid

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human respiratory epithelium and skin during primary infection; establishes lifelong latency in dorsal root/cranial nerve ganglia

identificationClues: Primary infection (varicella/chickenpox) causes a generalized vesicular rash in successive crops ("dew drops on a rose petal")
Reactivation (herpes zoster/shingles) produces a painful, dermatomal vesicular rash
PCR of vesicle fluid is the preferred confirmatory test
Live attenuated varicella vaccine and recombinant zoster vaccine are both available

diseases: Herpes zoster (shingles) — reactivation from dorsal root ganglia
Congenital varicella syndrome if maternal infection occurs early in pregnancy
clinicalImportance.transmission: Respiratory droplets and direct contact with vesicle fluid; highly contagious
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Routine childhood varicella vaccination has substantially reduced primary infection in vaccinating countries; herpes zoster risk increases with age and immunosuppression due to reactivation of latent virus
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Dermatomal distribution of the rash is a key clinical clue distinguishing zoster reactivation from other vesicular eruptions

examFacts.importantTest: PCR of vesicle fluid; Tzanck smear
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Same virus causes two distinct diseases: varicella on primary infection and zoster on later reactivation from ganglia
